<!--
House style for pull request bodies. Delete these comments as the sections fill in.

- Prose, not checkboxes. A reviewer reads top to bottom and comes away knowing what was wrong, what changed, and how it was checked.
- Written for someone outside this repo. No second person, no asides to the reader, no notes to the author.
- Numbers over adjectives: "225.7 MiB after a recursive listing of 9,230 objects" beats "memory looks fine".
- Headings are `##`, and only earn their place once the body carries more than one concern. A three-paragraph change is better as three paragraphs with no headings at all.
- Canonical names, so the corpus stays greppable: The fix, Verification, Scope. Add Symptom, Diagnosis or Why this shape when the story needs them. Not Tests, Testing or Validation, which all mean Verification.
- No hard wrapping. One paragraph per line.
- A stacked PR ends with its stack note under a `---` rule: the merge order, and why merge rather than squash.
-->

<!-- Lead paragraph, no heading: what is true today that should not be, and why it matters. -->

## The fix

<!-- What changed, and why this shape rather than the obvious alternative. -->

## Verification

<!-- What was run and what it showed: commands, counts, before and after. Say plainly when something was not checked. -->

## Scope

<!-- Optional. What this deliberately leaves undone, and where that belongs instead. -->
